title: Candy Corn Bag

drivers.name: Holiday: Thanksgiving (event week)
drivers.evidence: Historical median x0.49 vs baseline (2 occurrences), noise-adjusted.

drivers.name: Price increase (+6%)
drivers.evidence: Price increases typically reduce demand; no past data on this price, but similar increases show ~10% lift reduction in noisy data.

drivers.name: TikTok trend
drivers.evidence: Unverified but plausible; past viral events not captured in data; noise-adjusted estimate shrunk toward 1.0, so modest uplift.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 10.2. Thanksgiving historically suppresses sales (x0.49 vs baseline), but the product is trending on TikTok with a price increase to $4.08 (+6%). Past promotions show noise-adjusted lift of x1.45, but this is a price hike, not a discount. The TikTok trend may boost demand, but no past evidence of viral effects. The uplift model's suggestion of x0.49 ignores the price increase and trend. We adjust upward from x0.49 toward 1.0, but with thin evidence. Price increase likely dampens demand, and the TikTok trend is untested. No overlap with past events. Shrink toward 1.0 with medium confidence.

  median 10.2 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 25.6 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 19.8

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-85% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
